title: Preaching poor
hook: Dominic's answer to heresy was to live poor and preach well; later Dominicans also served the Inquisition

segments.voice: Yesterday, the innkeeper, and Dominic at his table in Toulouse until dawn. Your line was all night talking. Did you stay in a conversation longer than was comfortable? Day one thousand two hundred thirty.

The pope's envoys rode through the south of France the way important churchmen traveled: on good horses, with servants and baggage. They had been sent to win people back from the Cathars. And it wasn't working. People listened to the envoys, and then they looked at the Cathar preachers, who went on foot and lived plainly, and they compared. The envoys were ready to give up. Then they met two travelers from Spain, a bishop named Diego and his companion Dominic, and Diego gave them advice they didn't want to hear. Today, that advice, and the harder history that came after it.
screen: `GOOD HORSES, SERVANTS, BAGGAGE.` →`IT WASN'T WORKING.` → `ADVICE THEY DIDN'T WANT.`

segments.voice: Diego's advice, as Jordan of Saxony records it, was blunt. Send the horses home. Go on foot. Carry no gold or silver. Live and preach the way the apostles did, and let people see the Gospel before they hear it. It's the instruction Jesus gives his disciples in Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes." Diego didn't just say it. He sent his own household home and set out on foot, with Dominic beside him. They begged their food, slept where they could, and argued patiently in town squares and at kitchen tables, like the night at the inn. That is the seed of what Dominic later founded: the Order of Preachers, friars who would be poor so they could preach well, and study hard so they could preach truly. Now the harder part, and today asks us to hold it too. In the generations after Dominic, popes chose Dominican friars, along with Franciscans, to serve as inquisitors: judges in Church courts that tried people accused of heresy. Those courts used harsh methods, and some of the people they condemned were handed over to the civil authorities and put to death. That's part of the Dominican story, not a footnote to it. The Catholic Church has since asked God's forgiveness for violence used in the service of truth. Holding both means not choosing one memory. A bishop who sent his horses home. And the courts that came later, in the same habit. The order still carries both.
screen: `SEND THE HORSES HOME. GO ON FOOT.` · `POOR, SO THEY COULD PREACH WELL.` · `LATER DOMINICANS SERVED AS INQUISITORS.` · `THE ORDER CARRIES BOTH MEMORIES.` · then, large: `CARRY NEITHER PURSE, NOR SCRIP, NOR SHOES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold both. Settle, and breathe. Open one hand on your lap and place in it the picture of Diego and Dominic walking on foot, poor, arguing patiently at kitchen tables. Breathe. Open the other hand and place in it the courts that came later, the fear, and the people who were condemned. Don't close either hand. Breathe with both open. If you pray, you can pray for the people harmed in the name of faith, and for those who still try to preach poor. If you don't, just keep both hands open. The bell holds the time.
Preaching poor. Diego and Dominic's answer: no horses, no gold, the Gospel lived before it's spoken. Today's word.

Your line: poor preachers. Today, before you try to convince anyone of anything, leave one thing behind, the status, the credentials, the last word, and see if you're heard differently. Day one thousand two hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Dominican friars take vows of poverty, chastity and obedience and give themselves to study and preaching; Dominicans and other Catholics also speak openly today about the order's part in the Inquisition.

fork.setup: you're one of the pope's envoys. your preaching isn't working, and people keep comparing your horses with the plain-living Cathar preachers on foot. what do you do?
options: bring more guards and finer clothes.
send the horses home and preach on foot, poor.
fork.reveal: that was Diego's advice, and he went first, with Dominic beside him. it became the seed of the Order of Preachers.

original.note: Latin: the Order of Preachers, Dominic's name for his friars. it's why they sign OP.

trapdoor: what you thought: Dominicans are the Inquisition order.
what it means: an order begun by preachers who went poor and on foot, whose later friars also served as inquisitors. both are true.
what a scholar hears: Jordan of Saxony credits the plan to Bishop Diego at Montpellier: imitate the apostles, on foot, without gold or silver.

sources.quoted: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes

sources.ref: Jordan of Saxony, Libellus (Diego's advice to the legates at Montpellier)
Memory and Reconciliation: The Church and the Faults of the Past (International Theological Commission) and the Jubilee Day of Pardon prayers

notes: Jordan's account paraphrased: at Montpellier, Diego counseled the Cistercian legates to give up their retinues and preach on foot, without gold or silver, imitating the apostles, and set the example by sending his own household home. Confirm details, and that the envoys were discouraged ('ready to give up').

Inquisition: stated generally and without dates or numbers: popes chose Dominicans (and Franciscans) as inquisitors in the generations after Dominic; harsh methods; some condemned were handed to civil authorities and executed. The myth item 'Dominicans had no part in the Inquisition' is marked false. Confirm the wording is honest and fair to the order.

'The Catholic Church has since asked God's forgiveness for violence used in the service of truth' refers to the Day of Pardon (Jubilee 2000) prayers under John Paul II; date not stated. Confirm phrasing.
'The pope's envoys' are the papal legates (Cistercians, including Peter of Castelnau and Arnaud Amalric), not named. Confirm.
Douay-Rheims wording of Luke 10:4 to confirm.
howItsDone: confirm 'Dominicans ... speak openly today about the order's part in the Inquisition'.
